questions.stem: In India, 'headline inflation' is most commonly and officially measured for monetary policy purposes using which economic index?

options.option_text: Wholesale Price Index (WPI)
Consumer Price Index (CPI)
Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
Index of Industrial Production

questions.explanation: Since 2014, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officially adopted the Consumer Price Index (CPI - Combined) as the key measure of headline inflation to guide its monetary policy and interest rate decisions.

questions.stem: What exactly does the economic acronym 'WPI' stand for in the context of the Indian economy?

options.option_text: World Production Index
Weighted Price Indicator
Wholesale Price Index
Wage and Price Index

questions.explanation: WPI stands for Wholesale Price Index. It measures the changes in the prices of goods sold and traded in bulk by wholesale businesses to other businesses, rather than to everyday consumers.

questions.stem: Which official government organization in India is primarily responsible for compiling and publishing the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?

options.option_text: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Ministry of Finance directly
NITI Aayog (Think Tank) (alternative interpretation)
National Statistical Office (NSO)

questions.explanation: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is compiled and published monthly by the National Statistical Office (NSO), which operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

questions.stem: In the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) basket of India, which specific broad category of goods currently carries the highest overall weightage?

options.option_text: Primary Articles (Food)
Fuel and Power items
Manufactured Products
Services and IT goods

questions.explanation: The WPI basket is divided into three main groups. Manufactured Products carry the highest weight (over 64%). Primary Articles (like food and non-food agricultural items) carry about 22%, and Fuel & Power carry about 13%. (Services are NOT included in WPI).

questions.stem: Which specific mathematical economic formula for constructing a price index number strictly uses 'base year quantities' as its primary weights?

options.option_text: Paasche Index
Laspeyres Index
Fisher's Ideal Index
Marshall-Edgeworth Index

questions.explanation: The Laspeyres Price Index uses the quantities consumed in the base year as fixed weights (Formula: ΣP1Q0 / ΣP0Q0). The Paasche Index, on the other hand, uses current year quantities as weights (ΣP1Q1 / ΣP0Q1).

questions.stem: What is the base year for India's revised Index of Industrial Production (IIP) series currently used for all official releases?

options.option_text: Financial year 2004-05 (previously used base year)
Financial year 2011-12 (current official base year)
Financial year 2010-11 (used for interim estimates)
Financial year 2007-08 (used in GDP deflator)

questions.explanation: India revised the IIP base year from 2004-05 to 2011-12 in May 2017, aligning it with the new GDP and WPI base years. Option A (2004-05) was the old base and remains the most common wrong choice among students who recall the previous series.

questions.stem: In the CPI-Combined basket used for India's official inflation tracking, which expenditure group accounts for the single largest share of total weight?

options.option_text: Housing (includes rent, repairs, and maintenance)
Fuel and Light (cooking fuel and lighting needs)
Food and Beverages (cereals, milk, and vegetables)
Clothing, Bedding, and Footwear (textile goods)

questions.explanation: Food and Beverages carries approximately 54.18% weight in CPI-Combined (base 2012), reflecting India's household spending reality. Housing (10.07%) is often mistaken as the dominant group because it seems intuitively large in urban budgets, but it is far smaller than the food group in the combined index.

questions.stem: The Paasche Price Index is structurally distinct from the Laspeyres Price Index in that it uses which quantities as weights in its formula?

options.option_text: Base period quantities adjusted for income-level changes
Current period quantities prevailing in the comparison year
Geometric mean of base and current period quantities
Fixed quantities sourced from a decennial population census

questions.explanation: Paasche uses current year quantities (Qn) as weights: ΣPnQn / ΣP0Qn. Laspeyres uses base year quantities (Q0). Option A is a common confusion — neither index adjusts weights for income; they differ only in the time period of the quantity weights used.

questions.stem: In India's IIP framework (base year 2011-12), which sector carries the dominant weight of approximately 77.6% in the overall index?

options.option_text: Mining sector, covering extraction of coal and ores
Electricity sector, covering power generation output
Manufacturing sector, covering all factory production
Construction sector, covering buildings and bridges

questions.explanation: IIP covers three sectors: Manufacturing (~77.63%), Mining (~14.37%), and Electricity (~7.99%). Manufacturing's dominance means monthly IIP swings are almost entirely driven by factory output. Option D is a trap — Construction is tracked separately via the use-based 'Infrastructure/Construction Goods' sub-index, not as a standalone IIP sector.

questions.stem: Fisher's Ideal Price Index is considered 'ideal' among classical index formulas primarily because it simultaneously satisfies which two statistical tests?

options.option_text: The Unit Test and the Circular Test of index consistency
The Time Reversal Test and the Factor Reversal Test
The Chain Base Test and the Fixed Base Weighted Test
The Commodity Reversal Test and the Identity Test

questions.explanation: Fisher's Index = √(Laspeyres × Paasche). This geometric mean satisfies the Time Reversal Test (reversing base and current year gives the reciprocal) and the Factor Reversal Test (price index × quantity index = value ratio). Option A is wrong — neither Laspeyres nor Paasche satisfies the Circular Test, and Fisher's primary distinction is the two tests named in B.

questions.stem: In index number methodology, the statistical technique of 'splicing' is specifically applied when which situation arises in a long-run price series?

options.option_text: Price data for seasonal commodities is missing in certain months
Two index series with different base years must be linked into one continuous series
Geometric mean replaces arithmetic mean during a Laspeyres revision cycle
Basket weights are updated mid-series using newer consumption survey data

questions.explanation: Splicing links an old index series (e.g., WPI base 2004-05) to a new series (base 2011-12) by calculating a conversion factor at the overlap point, enabling a single unbroken time series for trend analysis. Option D describes 'rebasing' or 'chain-linking', which is a separate concept — rebasing updates weights but does not necessarily link two separate series into one.

questions.stem: Among the use-based categories in India's IIP, which sub-index is most closely watched as a leading indicator of private investment cycles despite being the most statistically volatile component?

options.option_text: Primary Goods index, tracking raw material and food output
Capital Goods index, tracking machinery and equipment output
Consumer Durables index, tracking household appliance output
Infrastructure Goods index, tracking cement and steel output

questions.explanation: Capital Goods production (boilers, turbines, machine tools) directly reflects new capacity creation by firms, making it a proxy for business investment sentiment. Its month-to-month swing can exceed ±30%, far outstripping other use-based categories. Consumer Durables (Option C) is frequently confused with Capital Goods; the key distinction is that durables track consumer spending on long-lived items, not producer-side investment in productive machinery.
